History class always felt so boring in school, but the actual stories behind it? Totally fascinating. Like, did you know that Cleopatra lived closer in time to the moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramids? That absolutely blows my mind every time I think about it.

The problem with how we learn history is it's all dates and names and "memorize this for the test." But the real stuff is way more interesting. People back then were just as messy and dramatic as we are now. Feuds, scandals, love affairs, terrible decisions made at two in the morning. Regular human stuff.

What really gets me is thinking about all the people who didn't make it into the history books. For every king or general we know about, there were millions of regular folks just trying to get by. What were their lives like? What did they worry about? Probably the same things we do. Bills, relationships, whether dinner was gonna turn out okay.

That's why I like history now, as an adult. It's basically just people being people, over and over, wearing different outfits. We haven't changed as much as we think.
